Record Class NamePattern

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.api.NamePattern
Record Components:
mode - matching algorithm to apply; null together with a null value is NamePattern.MatchMode.ANY
value - pattern string interpreted according to mode
public record NamePattern(NamePattern.MatchMode mode, String value) extends Record
A named string-matching predicate used by selectors to filter JVM operations by class name, method name, thread name, resource name, or any other string-valued attribute.

Five match modes are supported, in increasing power:

NamePattern match modes
ModeSemanticsExample
NamePattern.MatchMode.ANYAlways matches. No value needed. NamePattern.any()
NamePattern.MatchMode.EXACTFull string equality. NamePattern.exact("java.sql.Connection")
NamePattern.MatchMode.PREFIXString starts with value. NamePattern.prefix("io.lettuce")
NamePattern.MatchMode.GLOB* matches any sequence of characters, ? exactly one (one code point: a surrogate pair is one character, a line terminator is one too); every other character matches itself. NamePattern.glob("com.example.*.Repository")
NamePattern.MatchMode.REGEXFull Pattern match. NamePattern.regex(".*Service(Impl)?")

A null candidate string never matches any pattern except NamePattern.MatchMode.ANY.

A GLOB is matched directly, without a regex and without allocating. REGEX patterns are compiled once and cached in a JVM-wide bounded cache keyed by the pattern string (capacity 1024); a full cache is emptied before the next expression is cached, so a pattern-spamming plan cannot pin arbitrary heap and a plan's own expressions are cached again.

No input is silently reinterpreted: a mode other than NamePattern.MatchMode.ANY needs a non-blank value, NamePattern.MatchMode.ANY takes none (a null, blank or "*" value, kept as "*"), and a value needs a mode. Without both, the pattern is NamePattern.MatchMode.ANY.

  • Constructor Details

    • NamePattern

      public NamePattern(@Nullable NamePattern.MatchMode mode, @Nullable String value)
      Canonical constructor. Both null make NamePattern.MatchMode.ANY; NamePattern.MatchMode.ANY's value is always "*".
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the mode is not NamePattern.MatchMode.ANY and the value is null or blank, if the mode is NamePattern.MatchMode.ANY and the value is other than null, blank or "*", or if a value is given without a mode

  • Method Details

    • any

      public static NamePattern any()
      Returns a pattern that matches any string, including null. The standard choice when a selector field is not constrained. Returns a shared singleton, so selectors that use any() allocate nothing on the plan parsing path.
      Returns:
      a NamePattern that matches any name

    • exact

      public static NamePattern exact(String value)
      Returns a pattern that matches only strings exactly equal to value.
      Parameters:
      value - the exact string to match; must be non-blank
      Returns:
      a NamePattern matching the exact value

    • prefix

      public static NamePattern prefix(String value)
      Returns a pattern that matches strings starting with value. Efficient for package- prefix filtering (e.g., "io.lettuce" matches all Lettuce classes).
      Parameters:
      value - the prefix; must be non-blank
      Returns:
      a NamePattern matching names with the given prefix

    • glob

      public static NamePattern glob(String value)
      Returns a glob pattern where * matches any sequence of characters (line terminators included) and ? matches exactly one character (one code point); every other character, \ and regex metacharacters included, matches itself.

      Examples: "com.example.*.Repository", "worker-thread-?".

      Parameters:
      value - the glob expression; must be non-blank
      Returns:
      a NamePattern matching names with the given glob pattern

    • regex

      public static NamePattern regex(String value)
      Returns a full Pattern-based matcher applied against the entire candidate string (implicit ^...$ anchoring).
      Parameters:
      value - a valid Java regex; must be non-blank
      Returns:
      a NamePattern matching names with the given regex
      See Also:
      • Pattern.matches(String, CharSequence)

    • matches

      public boolean matches(@Nullable String candidate)
      Tests whether candidate matches this pattern.
      Parameters:
      candidate - the string to test; null matches only NamePattern.MatchMode.ANY
      Returns:
      true if the candidate satisfies this pattern
